course_description:
Using R, this course introduces students to the family of models that define the field of predictive analytics. Specific model forms introduced in the course include linear and logistic regression, neural networks, and recommendation systems. The focus is on developing an intuition for predictive modelling and knowledge of the essential concepts.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

Based on students' feedback from the previous semester, this course is becoming more practical and closer to machine learning concepts, specifically unsupervised/supervised machine learning technique.

course_aims: The broad aim of the course is to provide students with an indepth exposure to the methods of machine learning as they apply to business. Emphasis is placed on the established methods of machine learning, including tree-based methods and support vector machines. The course is applied in nature and makes extensive uses of R, which is open-source software for numerical analysis. The course is organised into four modules: preparation for machine learning, regression techniques for prediction and classification, machine learning techniques for prediction and classification, and machine learning methods for clustering. The more general goals of the course are to learn the language of machine learning, develop understanding of the key concepts in the application of machine learning, to develop appreciation of the application of machine learning business, and to develop an awareness of the policy and strategy implications of machine learning for business and beyond. The course builds on BSAN2204 Methods of Business Analytics and provides a context in which students can further develop their understanding of the R environment with a view towards becoming effective and professional business analysts.

learning_outcomes.description: Recognise and explain the role of machine learning for business.
Explain the key concepts in machine learning for business.

Compare and critically evaluate the methods of machine learning.
Demonstrate how applications of machine learning can inform and improve business performance.

assessment_details.title: Machine Learning Foundations Report (A1)
assessment_details.task_description: Students must apply predictive modelling methods to a dataset and recommend the best solution for a business problem. More specifically, they should prepare and clean dataset provided, build and tune linear regression, logistic regression, and tree-based models, and incorporate time series analysis where the data has a temporal structure. Students then compare model performance and justify their final recommendation. This is important because it gives students hands-on practice with the fundamentals of predictive modelling, building a foundation for next assignments. assessment_details.task_description: Students must complete an in-person quiz covering the concepts taught across the first half of the course. For example, answering questions on data preparation, linear and logistic regression, time series analysis, tree-based methods, support vector machines, clustering, ensemble methods, and unsupervised machine learning. It includes selecting and justifying the right method for a given business scenario. This is important because it independently verifies each student's own understanding under exam conditions. assessment_details.title: Advanced Machine Learning Project (A3)
assessment_details.task_description: Students must design and implement a dual model that combines unsupervised and supervised machine learning into one single pipeline. For example, using clustering or dimensionality reduction to segment customers or engineer novel features, then feeding that output into a supervised model that predicts a business outcome, before evaluating alternatives and presenting a clear, justified business recommendation. This is important because machine learning systems chain these stages rather than using them in isolation, so the task asks students to combine techniques from across the course into a single solution to a business problem.
